messages:
Maria G: Heads-up — rolling firmware+BIOS push in us-west1 started ~09:05. Provisioner shows ~4 racks stuck in 'provisioning' after BMC flash. Noticed secure_boot flag flipped to false on affected hosts. Anyone else seeing this?
Kevin L: Which images were pushed?
Maria G: firmware:v3.2.1, bios:2026-03-18 (defaults). Quick snippet from one host: 
```
# ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.0.12.3 -U admin -P **** sel elist
SEL# 00 | 03/18/26 09:07:22 | System Event | Sensor: Secure Boot | secure_boot changed: 1 -> 0
```
infra-bot: Canary deployed to r-12 at 09:05. Healthcheck failed at 09:11. Auto-rollback OFF (manual override).
Anya R: If secure_boot toggled off, our signed kernel isn't accepted -> provisioning fails early. We can try ipmi to flip it back but depends on BMC vendor support. Risk of bricking if persistent settings mismatch.
Sam H: Pause the rollout ASAP. Move provisioning traffic to eu1/dedicated pool to keep customers running. @kevin can you run rollback on affected racks?
Kevin L: Pausing now. Starting targeted rollback on r-12 and r-13. Running: 
```bash
./scripts/rollback_bmc_secureflag.sh --racks r-12,r-13 --timeout 600
```
Claire M: FYI shifting provisioning to eu1 will increase egress and cross-region costs. Rough calc: +$2.8k/day if backlog persists >6h.
Maria G: If rollback fails we'll need console/serial reflash for the rest. Oncall @Anya R can you request serial access and schedule KVM windows?
Anya R: Requested serial tickets. I'll attempt the ipmitool raw toggle first (vendor-specific). Example attempt: 
```
ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P $PASS raw 0x30 0x45 0x01 0x01 || echo "vendor unsupported"
```
infra-bot: Alert — provisioning queue length spiked to 12k jobs; autoscaler trying to allocate but GPU pool saturated. Recommendation: temporary reserved capacity bump or pause non-critical jobs.
Sam H: Confirmed pause of rollout. Kevin ETA ~10m for r-12/r-13 result.
Kevin L: Rollback completed on r-12: secure_boot now true, nodes are re-provisioning (r-12: 2/24 GPUs online so far). r-13 still failing — looks like BMC firmware returned corrupted NVRAM, serial required.
Maria G: Good progress. Filing immediate action items: 1) keep rollout paused, 2) prevent manual override of auto-rollback flag, 3) add a post-flash secure_boot verification probe to the pipeline, 4) open incident ticket.
Claire M: Also want an alert that maps provisioning backlog -> cost estimate so finance can see impact early. I can add a quick panel to the infra dashboard if you give me the metric.
Maria G: I'll attach the queue metric to a card. Creating incident INC-2026-1357 and adding runbook notes.
Kevin L: For the postmortem: capture BMC vendor, exact flash sequence, and which models exposed the EEROM flip. Also add an automated canary that validates secure_boot after each flash (small sample) before broad rollout.
Anya R: Oncall will handle serial reflashes for r-13/r-14 tonight if rollback scripts can't fix NVRAM. I'll coordinate time windows.
Maria G: Thanks everyone. Leaving rollout paused until we confirm r-14/r-15 via serial or rollback. Will post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
